question: Measure native retention on patch L110 under reduced categorical noise (cat_noise_level 0.25 and 0.5), with matched unguided controls. Prior L110 evidence at cat_noise_level 1.0 (R05) shows joint_formation 0.0, joint_at_integration 0.0, boundary_N_probability 0.005, boundary_C_probability 0.095, and retention_after_formation null, so no native suffix was formed or retained to measure. R06 (assignment_type_cost 0.5, same patch, cat_noise_level 1.0) partially restored formation (joint_formation 0.083, retention_after_formation 0.5) but with boundary_N_probability 0.204, indicating the N target at slot 12 is poorly supported. The requested reduced-noise values 0.25 and 0.5 have not been tested at this exact dose on L110; this is an explicit prospective hypothesis that lowering categorical noise will raise joint_formation and retention_after_formation above the R05/R06 levels. Falsifier: if matched unguided controls show equal or higher joint_formation and retention_after_formation than the guided runs at 0.25 and 0.5, the noise reduction is not the driver. Smallest discriminating test: run L110 at cat_noise_level 0.25 and 0.5 with matched unguided controls and compare joint_formation, retention_after_formation, and mean_pic50. Note: L110 is a counterfactual patch (source_score 8.912, targets N at 12 and C at 22); its native-suffix retention is only meaningful if formation occurs, and the R05 null retention reflects absent formation rather than measured loss.
